card.title: Design & control of a coaxial drone
card.imageAlt: Coaxial drone prototype during an indoor flight test

title: Design, Modeling, and Control of a Coaxial Drone
summary: A coaxial drone design combining two counter-rotating rotors with dual-axis thrust vectoring, supported by a nonlinear flight model and control strategy.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: A coaxial drone design combining two counter-rotating rotors with dual-axis thrust vectoring, supported by a nonlinear flight model and control strategy.
The compact platform uses two propellers and two servomotors. Its six-degree-of-freedom model and nonlinear control allocation are evaluated through numerical simulations and flight experiments.

images.alt: Coaxial drone prototype flying in an indoor test space
images.caption: The coaxial prototype during an indoor flight test.

sections.heading: Airframe and thrust vectoring
paragraphs: Two counter-rotating propellers share a common axis. Below them, two servomotors connected in series tilt the propulsion assembly about orthogonal axes, directing thrust for roll and pitch maneuvers without a cyclic swashplate.

The battery and electronics occupy the lower fuselage, placing the center of gravity below the tilting assembly. The structure view shows how the components connect; the three poses illustrate independent and combined servo motion.

images.alt: Mechanical structure and coordinate frames of the coaxial drone, showing the rotor assembly, two serial servomotors, center of gravity, and lower fuselage
images.caption: Airframe layout: coaxial rotors, two serial servos, and the lower fuselage.

images.alt: Three poses of the coaxial drone illustrating positive roll, combined roll and pitch, and positive pitch through its two servomotors
images.caption: Thrust vectoring through roll, combined roll and pitch, and pitch motion.

sections.heading: Modeling and control
paragraphs: A nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom model captures the coupled position and attitude dynamics. Control allocation converts the desired force and yaw torque into two rotor-speed commands and two servo angles. Position and yaw are regulated, with damping added to the remaining roll and pitch dynamics.

The controller runs at 250 Hz on an STM32F405. A 9-axis IMU and time-of-flight sensor provide attitude and distance measurements for height estimation, while Bluetooth carries setup commands and telemetry.

images.alt: Coaxial drone prototype beside close-up views of its STM32 flight controller, IMU, and time-of-flight sensor
images.caption: Custom flight hardware with the STM32 controller, IMU, and distance sensor.

sections.heading: Propulsion performance
paragraphs: Bench measurements compare the 10-inch coaxial propulsion system with a quadrotor using 5-inch propellers. The platform comparison establishes the tested geometry, while the power–thrust curves show its measured performance.
Within these tested configurations, the coaxial system requires less electrical power at the same thrust over the overlapping measurement range.

images.alt: Side-by-side photographs of the 10-inch coaxial drone and the quadrotor with 5-inch propellers used in propulsion testing
images.caption: Test platforms: 10-inch coaxial rotors and a quadrotor with 5-inch propellers.

images.alt: Measured electrical power versus thrust for the tested coaxial drone and quadrotor, with fitted trends
images.caption: Measured electrical power versus thrust for the two propulsion systems.

sections.heading: Flight validation
paragraphs: The custom STM32 platform demonstrates vertical ascent toward a commanded height using the proposed controller and combined distance/attitude feedback. The ascent logs show position error, attitude, actuator commands, and trajectory. Accumulated state-estimation errors limit stability during longer operation on this platform.

A separate hover trial uses a Pixhawk 4 mini with its embedded sensor fusion and existing control allocation. The hover logs provide an additional demonstration of the airframe, with approximately maintained position and attitude.

images.alt: Vertical ascent flight logs showing position tracking error, attitude, motor and servo commands, and the measured three-dimensional trajectory
images.caption: Custom controller: vertical ascent with position, attitude, actuator, and trajectory logs.

images.alt: Hover logs showing position, pitch roll and yaw, motor and servo outputs, and battery voltage over time
images.caption: Pixhawk 4 mini: a separate hover trial using its existing control allocation.
